This game is not for me. I played DotP 2012 hundreds of hours, same for 2013, and nearly a thousand hours with 2014. I skipped on the 2015 because I disliked it, and because I mainly play 2HG with friends (which was lacking in the 2015, and it was a dealbreaker for me).

Now, this Magic Duels: Origins thing. I like the UI, and most cosmetic changes they did. I would have liked to keep the "hold priority" option, but I don't resent losing it too much. We cannot "bluff" that we might have instants ready if there's a auto-continue selling the punchline. But, hey! It's not that bad.

Now, for the "free" part. It's dumb. I get it that WotC is in there for the money, but come on, this is ridiculous. You need to play an insane amount of time if you don't want to invest money in the game. On the other hand, if you want to unlock about everything, and are willing to pay for it, be prepared to hand over over fifty bucks. Eighty-something, told me a friend who did the math.

And this is only for the basic game. The expansions aren't out yet.

As for I, since I mainly play 2HG and that there is no coins in this kind of games, I cannot play the game the way I normally do (and which gives me the most fun) and earn coins to unlock cards too. So I'm in a lose-lose dynamic: either grind my way playing modes I don't care about, either pay big bucks for a game that would be 15$ max in my book - hey, I would gladly have paid 15$ for the basic game, and 10$ for the expansions, as it used to be with DotP. But to pay that much money for random cards, which will represent a slight percentage of the total amount of cards the game could offer, is the kind of thing that insult my intellect.

On a final note, there's no multiplayer game lobby anymore. This means that this game is made for people playing randoms strangers, not buddies playing together (even if we still can, we have to create a new game and invite each other every time). Somehow, I find this last detail depressing.

High ranking 2015 player here. What you're saying is mostly true.

Magic has gone pay to win. Some will argue that it hasn't, but the reality is that playing other players gives more coins per win, and people with a larger selection of cards have better odds. Boosters cost 150 coins, and you only earn 15 coins per win in solo play mode. This means you have to win 10 solo play games to get one 6 card booster. Multiplayer games net 20 coins per win and force you to win 8 games to get a booster with 10 coins left over.

2015 was actually a pretty good game. Apart from the missing two headed giants mode, and shoddy matchmaking implementation the rest of the game was pretty good and had a fairly large card selection. Why they dumped that interface for the crap in origins I'll never know.

Origins is a blatant cash grab, and a complete disservice to MtG fans.
